name: kdif
description: Interactive HTML diff of a KiCad board and schematic between git revisions
description_full:
kdif turns the git history of a KiCad project into a single self-contained interactive HTML file: the board layers and every schematic sheet of two revisions drawn on top of each other (red = only in A, green = only in B, yellow = unchanged), plus a crossfade slider, A/B views and a split view. Layers and sheets that actually changed are marked, so a review starts from what moved rather than from a wall of geometry.

The toolbar button opens a panel that already knows the project you have open: tick the commits to compare (short hash, date, subject and tag of every commit that touched the board or the schematic) and the layers to include - the two most recent commits and all layers are ticked for you - press Generate, and open the result when you want to look at it. The generated file has no external dependencies: attach it to a release or send it to a colleague.

Under the hood it drives kicad-cli and reads revisions straight out of the project's git repository (the working tree is never switched). git has to be installed; the same tool also works as a standalone command-line program - see the project homepage.
